chunks: Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Ishaq al-Taliqani - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id - the servant of the Hashemites - quoted on the authority of Ali ibn Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhdhal, on the authority of his father, 'I asked Al-Ridha (peace be upon him)'

about the meaning of 'Bismillah'. He said, 'The meaning of saying 'Bismillah' is that I put one of the marks of the Honorable, the Exalted God, that is servitude, on myself.' Then I asked him, 'What is the mark?' He replied, 'It means a sign.'
ai.seo_question: What is the theological meaning of 'Bismillah' according to Imam al-Rida?
ai.summary: In this tradition from *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida*, Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) interprets 'Bismillah' not merely as an invocation but as an ontological state where the believer bears the 'mark' (simah) of God, identified specifically as 'servitude' (ubudiyyah). This definition aligns with the Shia theological emphasis on *ubudiyyah* as the essential characteristic of creation, distinguishing the servant from the Creator while maintaining a profound connection to the Divine. The clarification that 'simah' means 'alamah' (sign) underscores the idea that true servitude is the visible and defining attribute of one who invokes God's name.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 26-19 Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Ishaq al-Taliqani - may God be pleased with him - narrated that ِAhmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa’eed - the servant of the Hashemites quoted on the authority of Ali ibn Al-Hassan ibn Ali ibn Fadhdhal, on the authority of his father, “I asked Al-Ridha (s) about the meaning of ‘In the Name of Allah.’”

Al-Ridha (s) said, ‘The meaning of saying ‘In the Name of Allah’ is that I put one of the marks of the Honorable the Exalted God that is His servitude on myself.’ Then I asked Al-Ridha (s) what is meant by ‘the mark of’?’ Al-Ridha (s) replied, ‘It means a sign of.’”
